question: What is the main reason for setting up an IV piggyback (IVPB)?

options.A: To rapidly drain excess blood volume
options.B: To deliver secondary intermittent medications
options.C: To measure direct central venous pressure
options.D: To provide total permanent nutrition

explanation: An IV piggyback lets you hang a smaller bag of medicine (like an antibiotic) to run alongside the main IV fluid bag without hassle.

question: What is the main job of the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN)?

options.A: Employing all newly graduated nurses directly
options.B: Setting international trade tariffs for medical supplies
options.C: Managing hospital budgets across all state capitals
options.D: Regulating standards of nursing education and practice

explanation: Correct! The NMCN sets the rules for nursing schools, issues our licenses, and keeps the profession standard and safe.

question: A nurse wants to improve maternal health in a rural area where many women use traditional birth attendants. What is the best approach regarding these attendants?

options.A: Ignore them completely and tell pregnant women never to speak to them
options.B: Ask them to close their businesses and work as hospital cleaners
options.C: Arrest them immediately for practicing medicine without a formal license
options.D: Engage and train them to recognize danger signs and refer women to the clinic

explanation: Working with traditional birth attendants builds a safe bridge instead of creating conflict, saving more mothers. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h4)

question: An adult patient's calculated BMI is 32.5. How do you classify this using WHO guidelines?

options.A: Obesity Class II
options.B: Overweight
options.C: Obesity Class I
options.D: Severe Obesity

explanation: You nailed it! A BMI landing between 30.0 and 34.9 falls under Obesity Class I.

question: Which injection site symptom means the patient needs to call a doctor right away?

options.A: A small pinprick dot of dry blood on the skin surface
options.B: Pus drainage, severe pain, and spreading warmth
options.C: Temporary slight coolness where the alcohol dried
options.D: Mild fading skin discoloration from a tiny bruise

explanation: Those are classic red flags for an infection! Pus, severe pain, and warmth mean the site needs medical attention quickly.

question: Which of these personal items must kitchen staff take off before they start working?

options.A: Non-slip kitchen shoes
options.B: Hairnets and caps
options.C: Clean cotton aprons
options.D: Rings and wristwatches

explanation: Rings and watches trap dirt and hidden bacteria that are tough to wash away. Taking them off keeps the kitchen truly clean!

question: Which animal is known as the natural reservoir host for the Ebola virus?

options.A: Pigs on farms
options.B: Domestic dogs
options.C: Fruit bats
options.D: Cattle and goats

explanation: Spot on! Fruit bats carry the virus naturally without getting sick themselves. Think of them as the original home of the virus in nature.

question: Which muscle type is attached to your skeleton and under your conscious control?

options.A: Visceral muscle
options.B: Cardiac muscle
options.C: Smooth muscle
options.D: Skeletal muscle

explanation: Skeletal muscles are the ones you choose to move when you walk, dance, or lift objects.

question: Which of these is a common biological reason for sexual dysfunction in older women?

options.A: Hyperactive thyroid function
options.B: Hormonal shifts during menopause
options.C: Excessive pelvic muscle tone
options.D: Increased production of estrogen

explanation: You've got it! Lower estrogen levels during menopause can cause dryness and tissue changes, which sometimes make things a bit uncomfortable.

question: A charge nurse creates the weekly duty roster and assigns patient loads for the morning shift. What type of plan is this?

options.A: Strategic plan
options.B: Visionary plan
options.C: Operational plan
options.D: Tactical plan

explanation: Duty rosters and daily patient assignments are classic examples of short-term operational planning at the unit level. [learn more](GST321_U1_T6#GST321_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a good reason to be careful with the Kubler-Ross model?

options.A: It guarantees every patient will have a completely painless death
options.B: Treating the stages as strict rules can hurt individualized care
options.C: It might miss cultural differences in how people grieve
options.D: Patients often skip or repeat stages

explanation: Spot on! The model maps out emotions—it has nothing to do with curing physical pain or guaranteeing a pain-free passing.

question: What is the main job of the large intestine in our daily digestion?

options.A: Producing bile to break down fats
options.B: Absorbing water and compacting waste
options.C: Secreting digestive enzymes for proteins
options.D: Mixing food with stomach acid

explanation: As food waste travels through, the large intestine pulls out the remaining water, turning liquid into solid stool. Spot on!

question: Why can keeping patient information private be tricky in a home setting?

options.A: Patients demand that all their lab results be broadcasted
options.B: Medical records must be pasted publicly on the front door
options.C: Home health nurses are not legally bound by privacy laws
options.D: Extended family members and neighbors are often present around the living area

explanation: Well reasoned! Open living spaces and bustling family compounds mean we have to be extra careful about who might overhear our discussions.

question: What is a protective factor for mental health?

options.A: Strong family and social support systems
options.B: A family history of severe psychiatric illness
options.C: Experiencing severe trauma during childhood
options.D: Growing up in an environment of chronic poverty

explanation: Protective factors like social support help shield individuals from stress and lower the likelihood of mental health problems. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h3)

question: What is a major hurdle when introducing telehealth gadgets to home care patients?

options.A: Internet access is legally banned in residential areas
options.B: Physicians refuse to look at remote monitoring data
options.C: Lack of digital literacy among patients and families
options.D: Telehealth devices completely eliminate all illnesses

explanation: Many patients—especially older adults—might feel intimidated by tablets or apps until you patiently walk them through it step by step.

question: Which organ system is the hero for excreting non-volatile (fixed) metabolic acids from the body?

options.A: The lungs
options.B: The kidneys
options.C: The liver
options.D: The stomach

explanation: While the lungs handle volatile acids like $CO_2$, the kidneys take care of the heavy lifting by filtering out fixed metabolic acids in the urine.

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for triggering the milk ejection or let-down reflex during breastfeeding?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Oxytocin causes the tiny muscles around the milk glands to squeeze, pushing the milk down the ducts so the baby can drink it easily. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h1)

question: Why does fluid and waste build up in the body during an episode of Acute Glomerulonephritis?

options.A: The bladder becomes too weak to push urine out
options.B: Too much water is produced directly inside the liver
options.C: Inflamed filtering units fail to clean the blood properly
options.D: The ureters completely block the flow of urine

explanation: When glomeruli become swollen and inflamed, their normal filtering function drops, causing fluid and waste products to accumulate in the body. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T4#GNS213_U4_T4_h1)

question: How do deep, slow breathing exercises physically help a patient calm down?

options.A: They increase skeletal muscle tension to release trapped toxins
options.B: They permanently block the adrenal glands from producing cortisol
options.C: They flood the bloodstream with extra adrenaline to burn off energy
options.D: They stimulate the vagus nerve to activate the parasympathetic nervous system

explanation: Deep breathing acts like a brake pedal for your nervous system, stimulating the vagus nerve to switch you from 'fight-or-flight' to 'rest-and-digest.' [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h7)

question: Which physical health condition is commonly linked to the chronic stress of long-term unemployment?

options.A: Hypertension
options.B: Sickle cell anemia
options.C: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.D: Type 1 Diabetes

explanation: Correct! Ongoing stress from financial worry keeps the body's stress response switched on, which can raise blood pressure over time. Keep up the great work! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T18#GNS225_U5_T18_h2)

question: What is the main job of hormones in our bodies?

options.A: Generate fast electrical impulses for muscle movement
options.B: Fight off bacterial infections in the bloodstream
options.C: Digest food particles inside the stomach lumen
options.D: Act as chemical messengers to regulate body functions

explanation: Think of hormones as the body's postal service! They are chemical messengers sent out by glands to travel through the blood and help manage how different organs work. You've got this!

question: If a patient has too much sodium in their blood, where does water naturally rush to?

options.A: Out of the blood vessels completely through the skin
options.B: From the interstitial spaces into the lymphatic system
options.C: From the extracellular space directly into the cells
options.D: From inside the cells into the extracellular space

explanation: Water loves to follow salt! High sodium outside pulls water right out of the cells, making them shrink. Physics and nursing working together!

question: How does chloride rushing into brain cells help calm the nervous system?

options.A: It blocks the release of oxygen from nearby red blood cells
options.B: It depolarizes the cell membrane to speed up reflex pathways
options.C: It stops the production of cellular energy molecules in mitochondria
options.D: It hyperpolarizes the cell membrane, making electrical firing less likely

explanation: When negative chloride ions flood the inside of the cell, it becomes 'hyperpolarized'—meaning it's much harder for runaway electrical signals to trigger it.

question: Why is incineration the go-to method for body parts and human tissues?

options.A: It completely destroys anatomical parts safely and respectfully through high heat
options.B: It turns biological tissues into safe fertilizer for crops
options.C: It allows tissues to be recycled into new plastic products
options.D: It is the cheapest way to produce electricity

explanation: High-heat incineration is a safe, hygienic way to dispose of anatomical waste while treating human remains with proper dignity.

question: Why are immediate drug reactions so dangerous?

options.A: They cannot be written in the patient chart
options.B: They only happen with kidney failure
options.C: They develop suddenly and can quickly become life-threatening
options.D: They never respond to emergency drugs

explanation: Because they happen so fast, you have very little time to act. That's what makes them true medical emergencies!

question: Why do we wait to find out the exact name of the poison instead of panicking right away?

options.A: Laboratory tests are always inaccurate in the first hour
options.B: Immediate life threats must be managed to prevent death
options.C: Hospital policy forbids asking family members about pill bottles
options.D: The poison usually breaks down and cannot be identified later

explanation: Spot on! If a patient's airway is blocked or their heart stops, knowing the chemical name of the poison won't save them. We stabilize life first, investigate second.

question: Which nursing diagnosis is most appropriate for a patient suffering from constant urine leakage caused by a fistula?

options.A: Risk for infection
options.B: Ineffective airway clearance
options.C: Impaired physical mobility
options.D: Deficient fluid volume

explanation: Constant exposure to urine on the perineal skin creates a very high risk for localized skin breakdown and severe infection. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T16#GNS312_U1_T16_h5)

question: Why is it dangerous to just silence an infusion pump alarm and walk away?

options.A: Unresolved alarms cause the pump to reverse fluid flow into the bag
options.B: It can delay necessary treatment or fail to catch a dangerous blockage
options.C: Hospital policy fines staff members who touch alarms too quickly
options.D: The pump will automatically erase all patient data if silenced

explanation: You got it! Alarms are there for a reason. Ignoring them without fixing the root cause can leave your patient without their meds or miss a serious line problem.

question: A community health nurse wants to understand why local women rarely attend hypertension screening camps. What is the best initial action?

options.A: Close the screening camp and open a men's health clinic
options.B: Report the community to the ministry of health immediately
options.C: Assume women do not care about their heart health
options.D: Hold focus groups with local women to discuss their barriers

explanation: Engaging directly with the affected population through focus groups uncovers the real reasons behind low attendance. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T22#GNS225_U5_T22_h7)

question: An older adult has had a nagging cough and hoarseness for three months that won't go away. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Instruct the patient to purchase over-the-counter cough syrup
options.B: Advise the patient to return only if they cough up blood
options.C: Report these findings to the clinician for further diagnostic evaluation
options.D: Reassure the patient that common colds often last for several months

explanation: Great clinical thinking! A cough that lasts that long without healing is a classic warning sign that needs a proper doctor's assessment right away.

question: A child eats enough daily calories from starchy grains like maize or cassava, but still has severe anemia. What economic factor is likely behind this?

options.A: Too much household spending on medical insurance
options.B: Inability to afford protein and micronutrient-dense foods
options.C: High local agricultural productivity driving down grain value
options.D: Excessive availability of fresh vegetables in local markets

explanation: Getting enough calories for energy isn't the same as getting rich nutrients. Without money for protective foods, deficiencies like anemia happen.

question: Maternal education in Nigeria is most closely linked to which of these health outcomes?

options.A: Cost of private health insurance
options.B: Frequency of major surgical operations
options.C: Availability of hospital bed spaces
options.D: Child immunization and nutrition rates

explanation: Correct! Educated mothers are generally better positioned to access preventive child healthcare and practice good infant nutrition.

question: Which brain pathway is mainly responsible for positive symptoms of psychosis, like hearing voices or seeing things?

options.A: Mesocortical pathway
options.B: Mesolimbic pathway
options.C: Tuberoinfundibular pathway
options.D: Nigrostriatal pathway

explanation: When the mesolimbic pathway becomes hyperactive, it drives those 'positive' symptoms like hallucinations. That's why antipsychotics target this specific area!

question: An elderly patient with failing eyesight is getting ready to go home from the hospital. Which home safety tip should you recommend first?

options.A: Replace all traditional doorbells with standard low-volume chimes.
options.B: Remove loose scatter rugs and ensure all hallways are brightly lit.
options.C: Install heavy dark curtains to block out harsh sunlight completely.
options.D: Store all household cleaning supplies inside the bedroom wardrobe.

explanation: Falls are a huge risk for patients with low vision. Clearing out tripping hazards like loose rugs and keeping hallways bright makes their home environment much safer!

question: Which animal vector transmits the parasite that causes malaria?

options.A: Female Anopheles mosquito
options.B: Domestic housefly
options.C: Freshwater blackfly
options.D: Multimammate rat

explanation: Malaria parasites are transmitted to humans through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h3)

question: How should a nurse view providing reproductive health education to teenagers?

options.A: As a punishment for teenagers who break hospital visiting rules
options.B: As an unnecessary task that encourages bad behavior in schools
options.C: As a duty that should be left entirely to traditional village leaders
options.D: As an essential health intervention that prevents dangerous complications

explanation: Reproductive health education is a core preventive service that safeguards young lives and promotes informed decision-making. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T4#GNS312_U4_T4_h5)

question: Which piece of advice should a nurse give a patient to prevent food and drug mix-ups?

options.A: Take all medications with grapefruit juice to help speed up absorption in the stomach
options.B: Check with your healthcare provider before starting any new herbal or over-the-counter products
options.C: Crush all of your tablets together in the morning to make them easier to swallow with juice
options.D: Stop taking your prescribed medications whenever you feel completely back to normal

explanation: Always remind patients to ask an expert before mixing everyday supplements, herbs, or shop-bought meds with their hospital prescriptions. Safety first!

question: What is the main purpose of a 'disease-modifying' drug?

options.A: To replace lost vitamins in the bloodstream
options.B: To give instant relief from sudden, sharp pain
options.C: To slow down how fast the disease damages the body
options.D: To completely cure the genetic mutation

explanation: Great job! Disease-modifying drugs don't fix everything overnight, but they work behind the scenes to alter the disease process and protect cells from further damage.

question: Which of these is NOT a safe way to treat drinking water?

options.A: Adding appropriate chlorine treatment
options.B: Boiling it thoroughly
options.C: Storing it uncovered in a warm, dusty corner
options.D: Using a certified water filtration system

explanation: Exactly! Leaving clean water uncovered is an open invitation for dust, flies, and germs to sneak right back in and contaminate it.

question: How can extreme poverty drive some families to practice early marriage?

options.A: By allowing the young bride to immediately secure high-paying employment
options.B: By guaranteeing free government housing for the newly wed couple
options.C: By reducing household financial burdens and sometimes yielding a bride price
options.D: By eliminating all taxes for families with married daughters

explanation: You got it! In severe economic hardship, some families feel pressured to marry off daughters to reduce mouths to feed or to gain financial help from a bride price.

question: Which skin preparation practice is essential before performing an intraarticular puncture?

options.A: Applying warm lotion to soften the skin surface
options.B: Shaving the entire limb hair without any cleanser
options.C: Wiping the skin clean with a dry cotton ball only
options.D: Allowing the antiseptic solution to dry completely on the skin

explanation: Antiseptic agents need time to dry so they can fully kill microbes on the skin surface before the needle enters. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h6)

question: How does severe anaemia affect the uterus while a woman is in active labor?

options.A: It makes the cervix open twice as fast.
options.B: It blocks blood flow through the umbilical cord.
options.C: It causes the water bag to break immediately.
options.D: It deprives the hardworking womb muscle of oxygen, leading to poor contractions.

explanation: Just like any muscle working hard at the gym, the uterus needs good oxygen to push effectively. Anaemia makes that tough!

question: What type of cartilage connects the bones in a symphysis joint, like the pubic symphysis?

options.A: Elastic cartilage
options.B: Calcified bone matrix
options.C: Fibrocartilage
options.D: Dense fibrous connective tissue

explanation: Spot on! Symphysis joints use tough pads of fibrocartilage to absorb shocks while giving just a tiny bit of flexibility.

question: What is the main job of a supercomputer in medical research?

options.A: Displaying continuous bedside vital sign waveforms
options.B: Printing hospital administrative billing invoices
options.C: Running daily electronic charting for individual patient rooms
options.D: Performing complex calculations for research like genomic sequencing

explanation: Spot on! Supercomputers are extreme number-crunchers used for massive scientific breakthroughs like decoding human genes.

question: Which of these is NOT a good step when setting up a clean workspace on a household table?

options.A: Washing your hands thoroughly before touching any supplies
options.B: Using a clean disposable barrier like a paper towel as your work surface
options.C: Keeping clean supplies separate from used or dirty items
options.D: Spraying the table with a standard household bleach solution right before laying down sterile instruments

explanation: Spray bottles and wet chemicals right next to open supplies can easily contaminate your clean field. Using a dry paper towel barrier is much safer!

question: How should a nurse collect a urine sample from a patient with a catheter?

options.A: By disconnecting the catheter tubing from the drainage bag
options.B: From the rubber sampling port using a sterile syringe
options.C: By squeezing urine backward from the tubing into the bladder
options.D: From the bottom valve of the plastic collection bag

explanation: Always use the special needleless sampling port with a sterile syringe. Never take urine from the drainage bag, as those germs have been sitting there and won't give an accurate lab result!

question: Why are awake COVID-19 patients sometimes asked to lie on their stomachs (prone positioning)?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for oxygen therapy
options.B: It makes it easier to insert nasogastric feeding tubes
options.C: It improves lung expansion and oxygen exchange
options.D: It prevents patients from developing pressure ulcers

explanation: Proning helps open up parts of the lungs that usually get squished, helping the patient breathe much better. Every day you're building clinical skills! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T12#GNS214_U1_T12_h5)

question: What are the three core parts of the epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Bacteria, virus, and fungi
options.B: Agent, host, and environment
options.C: Prevention, treatment, and cure
options.D: Patient, doctor, and nurse

explanation: Spot on! Think of it as a three-way puzzle: the germ (agent), the person (host), and their surroundings (environment). Keep building that foundation!

question: Which of the following is a primary advantage of the sublingual route?

options.A: Zero risk of side effects
options.B: No need for blood circulation
options.C: Longer duration than injections
options.D: Rapid onset of action

explanation: Direct absorption into blood vessels gives sublingual medicines a very fast therapeutic effect. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h4)

question: Why is proper health care waste management strictly regulated in clinical settings?

options.A: To ensure the facility uses less electricity every month
options.B: To make hospital compounds look neat for visiting inspectors
options.C: To prevent the spread of infections and protect community health
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing office supplies

explanation: Strict rules are necessary because improperly managed medical waste can transmit dangerous diseases to staff, patients, and the public. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h1)

question: What is the primary goal of nursing care during a psychiatric or behavioral emergency?

options.A: Proving the patient is at fault for their behavior
options.B: Immediately discharging the patient to home
options.C: Starting long-term psychotherapy in the emergency bay
options.D: Ensuring safety and de-escalating the crisis

explanation: Keeping everyone safe and calming the patient down is always your first priority in any mental health emergency. You've got this!

question: Why is building trust with the community so vital during an Ebola outbreak?

options.A: It stops the virus from becoming airborne
options.B: It lets the government cancel travel bans
options.C: It prevents families from hiding sick relatives and encourages early reporting
options.D: It gives clinic staff higher pay

explanation: Correct! When people trust health workers, they bring sick family members in early instead of hiding them, which stops the spread.

question: Which nursing action is an absolute must for a patient on a continuous paralytic drip in the ICU?

options.A: Applying lubricating eye drops and taping the eyelids shut
options.B: Encouraging the patient to perform deep breathing exercises hourly
options.C: Removing physical restraints so the patient can stretch their legs
options.D: Keeping the room completely dark so the patient can sleep deeply

explanation: Paralyzed patients can't blink, so their eyes dry out fast! Regular eye care prevents painful corneal scratches. You're thinking like a real nurse already!

question: Why is it important for the family to have a direct contact number for the psychiatric ward during a patient's leave?

options.A: So they can order extra hospital meals to be delivered
options.B: So they can negotiate a discount on hospital bills
options.C: So they can seek immediate guidance before minor challenges escalate into major crises
options.D: So they can report local weather conditions to the doctor

explanation: Having a direct phone line gives families peace of mind and lets them get professional advice before small issues become big problems.

question: At what point must the surgical time-out be done?

options.A: When the patient first arrives at the hospital gate
options.B: During the patient discharge counseling session
options.C: Just before the surgical incision is made
options.D: After the surgical wound has been fully closed

explanation: The time-out is our final safety pause right before the knife touches the skin, giving the whole team a chance to confirm everything is correct.

question: Which of these conditions is a true medical emergency involving sudden, dangerous swelling of the upper airway?

options.A: Benign nasal polyps
options.B: Chronic otitis media
options.C: Simple viral rhinitis
options.D: Acute epiglottitis

explanation: The epiglottis is the flap that guards your windpipe. When it swells up rapidly, it can completely block breathing, making it a critical emergency that needs immediate medical attention.

question: What is the most crucial piece of history to get when assessing a patient with suspected food poisoning?

options.A: A detailed list of all foods eaten in the last few days
options.B: Their childhood vaccination records
options.C: The brand name of their daily vitamins
options.D: Their travel history from the last ten years

explanation: Brilliant! To track down the culprit, we need to retrace what they've been eating recently. Nursing assessment 101—you're doing great!

question: Why do multiple humanitarian agencies need to work together during a major refugee crisis?

options.A: International agencies prefer to work in complete isolation from locals.
options.B: Government health ministries are legally banned from helping refugees.
options.C: It eliminates the need for any professional nursing staff on site.
options.D: No single organization has all the resources required to meet complex needs.

explanation: Crises are massive! Providing shelter, clean water, food, and healthcare all at once requires teamwork and pooled resources from many different organizations.

question: Why do we use computer software in clinical nursing today?

options.A: To replace the need for professional clinical judgment entirely
options.B: To help organize care, reduce errors, and streamline communication
options.C: To increase the time nurses spend filling out paper documents
options.D: To eliminate the requirement for direct patient interaction

explanation: You've got this! Software tools are just there to help make your data handling easier and more accurate, giving you more time for what really matters—caring for your patients. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h1)

question: What is the main job of the 'statement of the problem' in your proposal?

options.A: To list the names of every nurse working on the ward
options.B: To summarize the final conclusions of the study
options.C: To highlight the exact gap or issue requiring research
options.D: To advertise new medical equipment to the hospital

explanation: The problem statement tells your reader: 'Here is what we don't know yet, and here is why our study needs to fix it!'

question: What does the SBAR acronym stand for during a patient handover?

options.A: Symptoms, Breathing, Activity, Recovery
options.B: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.C: Safety, Blood, Airway, Respiration
options.D: Staff, Beds, Ambulances, Reports

explanation: Easy peasy! SBAR stands for Situation, Background, Assessment, and Recommendation. It keeps your shift handovers clear and professional.

question: What is the primary purpose of administering furosemide to a patient with acute renal failure and fluid overload?

options.A: To permanently repair damaged glomeruli in the nephrons
options.B: To dissolve large kidney stones blocking the ureters
options.C: To lower dangerous levels of blood glucose in the body
options.D: To stimulate urine output and reduce excess body fluid

explanation: Loop diuretics like furosemide help the kidneys excrete excess water and sodium when the patient is fluid overloaded. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T6#GNS213_U4_T6_h5)

question: In many Nigerian homes, what hazardous substance is most commonly swallowed by young children by accident because it was stored in an empty soft drink bottle?

options.A: Kerosene
options.B: Dry fertilizer
options.C: Carbon monoxide
options.D: Surgical spirit

explanation: Spot on! Kerosene is widely used for cooking and lighting. When poured into empty soft drink bottles, kids easily mistake it for a drink and swallow it. Always remember to teach parents to use proper, labeled containers!

question: If a patient has a large left-sided tension pneumothorax, which way is the trachea likely to shift?

options.A: Tracheal deviation toward the left side
options.B: Downward displacement of the liver
options.C: Tracheal deviation toward the right side
options.D: No movement of the mediastinal structures

explanation: Think of it like a crowded room: pressure builds up on the left and pushes everything over toward the healthy right side. You're building solid emergency nursing instincts!

question: Why is keeping things strictly confidential vital for youth-friendly health services?

options.A: Government insurance schemes refuse to pay claims if patient names are published
options.B: Traditional leaders demand exclusive rights to review all clinic patient logs
options.C: Fear of social stigma and exposure will drive young people to seek unsafe, clandestine alternatives
options.D: Hospitals lack physical filing cabinets to store confidential adolescent records

explanation: Exactly! If young people are afraid their families or communities will find out, they'll stay away from clinics and risk unsafe options. Privacy saves lives!

question: Which part of the brain acts like an alarm clock to keep us physically awake?

options.A: The peripheral nervous system
options.B: The spinal cord reflex arcs
options.C: The Ascending Reticular Activating System
options.D: The cerebellum and basal ganglia

explanation: Think of the ARAS as the brain's main power switch or alarm clock, sending constant wake-up signals from the brainstem to keep the cerebral cortex alert.

question: What is a simple, cheap way villagers can stop themselves from swallowing Guinea worm larvae in their drinking water?

options.A: Adding tablespoons of cooking oil to the water
options.B: Exposing the water bucket to direct moonlight
options.C: Stirring the water vigorously with a wooden spoon
options.D: Filtering water through a clean cloth

explanation: You got it! A simple cloth filter catches the tiny fleas carrying the larvae. Public health nursing is often about simple, effective tools!

question: What is the main benefit of using the 'teach-back' method during patient education?

options.A: It reduces the cost of buying medical equipment for the clinic
options.B: It measures the exact blood pressure of the client instantly
options.C: It eliminates the need for any further nursing documentation
options.D: It confirms whether the person truly understands the instructions

explanation: Brilliant! Asking patients to explain things back in their own words helps you catch and clear up any confusion before they leave.

question: What is a major challenge associated with the rapid adoption of new healthcare technologies?

options.A: Increased risk of user fatigue and software distraction
options.B: A total lack of interest from patients and families
options.C: The elimination of all medical errors in hospitals
options.D: Decreased need for cybersecurity measures

explanation: Poorly designed technology and excessive screen time can lead to digital fatigue and distract clinicians from direct patient interaction. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h6)

question: What does the medical acronym SUDEP stand for in epilepsy?

options.A: Sudden unexpected death in epilepsy
options.B: Severe unprovoked disorder of electrical pathways
options.C: Spontaneous upper digestive episode pathology
options.D: Secondary unstable depression and epilepsy

explanation: SUDEP refers to the rare and tragic sudden death of a person with epilepsy where no other clear cause can be found. Keep up your steady study routine! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T12#GNS222_U4_T12_h8)

question: Which of these is a realistic, patient-centered nutrition goal?

options.A: Walking for twenty minutes after lunch four days a week
options.B: Losing twenty kilograms by the end of this month
options.C: Eating a much healthier diet starting immediately
options.D: Eliminating all food cravings within forty-eight hours

explanation: Brilliant! This goal is specific, achievable, and easy to measure. Small, steady steps lead to big wins.

question: Why is drinking enough water important for protecting a susceptible host?

options.A: It directly destroys bacterial cell walls in the bloodstream
options.B: It replaces the need for standard vaccinations
options.C: It permanently eliminates all body toxins
options.D: It keeps mucosal membranes moist to trap foreign particles

explanation: Simple and natural! Well-hydrated mucous membranes in your nose and throat act like sticky traps to catch germs before they enter.

question: What best describes disease surveillance in public health?

options.A: A one-time survey conducted during a major crisis
options.B: A clinical trial testing new hospital equipment
options.C: A research study on the cure for chronic diseases
options.D: An ongoing and systematic collection of health data

explanation: Surveillance requires continuous monitoring and data gathering over time, unlike a single survey or short-term research trial. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h1)

question: What is the main goal of triage in a busy healthcare setting?

options.A: To sort patients and prioritize care based on urgency
options.B: To provide a complete medical diagnosis for every visitor
options.C: To collect insurance and billing information before treatment
options.D: To discharge minor cases without letting them see a doctor

explanation: Triage acts as your first safety filter when the ward is busy, ensuring the sickest patients get seen without dangerous delays. You've got this!

question: Where do isolation precautions mostly try to break the chain of infection?

options.A: At the mode of transmission
options.B: At the patient's genetic code
options.C: Inside the patient's bloodstream
options.D: Inside the pharmacy storage room

explanation: Barriers like masks, gloves, and private rooms primarily stop germs from traveling from one place to another. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h2)

question: Which processing method destroys all microorganisms, including bacterial spores?

options.A: Cleaning
options.B: Sterilization
options.C: Disinfection
options.D: Sanitization

explanation: Sterilization is the only process that completely eliminates every form of microbial life, including highly resistant bacterial spores. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h6)

question: Where are the large circumvallate papillae usually found on the tongue?

options.A: Scattered across the center
options.B: In a V-shape at the back
options.C: Along the lateral edges
options.D: At the very front tip

explanation: If you look way back on the tongue, circumvallate papillae form a neat V-shaped row packed with lots of taste buds.

question: How are Wernicke encephalopathy and Korsakoff syndrome related?

options.A: They are completely unrelated disorders affecting different organs
options.B: Korsakoff syndrome always occurs years before Wernicke develops
options.C: Wernicke is a mild form of memory loss caused by normal aging
options.D: Wernicke is the acute stage and Korsakoff is the chronic stage

explanation: They are actually two sides of the same coin! Wernicke is the sudden, early emergency phase, and Korsakoff is the long-term memory issue that follows if it's not treated quickly.

question: What is meant by 'brain drain' in the context of Nigerian healthcare staffing?

options.A: The mental fatigue caused by working night shifts
options.B: The gradual decline of memory in elderly patients
options.C: The migration of trained nurses to seek jobs abroad
options.D: The loss of patient records due to poor computer systems

explanation: Brain drain refers to skilled professionals leaving their home country for better opportunities overseas. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h8)

question: What is the most critical thing a nurse should teach a patient being discharged with chronic primary adrenal insufficiency?

options.A: How and when to administer emergency injectable hydrocortisone during acute stress or illness
options.B: Why strenuous physical exercise must be completely avoided for the rest of the patient's life
options.C: How to restrict daily dietary salt intake to prevent sudden spikes in blood pressure
options.D: Why it is safe to stop taking daily oral steroids once physical strength and appetite return

explanation: Teaching a patient how to use an emergency injection can literally save their life if a sudden crisis hits when they are far from a hospital.

question: What is the main difference between short-acting and long-acting corticosteroids?

options.A: How long they remain active in the body and their strength.
options.B: Whether they require a doctor's prescription.
options.C: If they cause weight gain during long-term therapy.
options.D: Whether they are swallowed or injected into a muscle.

explanation: You got it! Different steroid types stay in the system for different lengths of time and have varying strengths for reducing swelling.

question: Which condition is considered a high-risk factor that rules out a safe home delivery?

options.A: A normal vertex presentation at term
options.B: A history of a previous cesarean section
options.C: A history of a single normal spontaneous vaginal birth
options.D: A maternal age between twenty and thirty

explanation: Previous uterine scars carry a risk of uterine rupture during labor, making hospital delivery mandatory. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h2)

question: What is the primary function of a computer?

options.A: Manipulating and processing data
options.B: Storing physical hospital records
options.C: Generating electrical power
options.D: Replacing human clinical judgment

explanation: A computer is fundamentally designed to accept, store, and process raw data into usable information. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T5#GNS113_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why do pelvic organ prolapse conditions often lead to problems with urination?

options.A: Estrogen surges cause the bladder to double in physical size
options.B: Infection destroys the smooth muscle tissue of the ureters
options.C: The kidneys stop producing urine due to chronic pelvic pressure
options.D: The shifted position of the organs changes normal urine flow mechanics

explanation: When supportive pelvic structures weaken and sag, organs like the bladder shift out of place. This makes it hard to empty the bladder fully, leading to frequent urges or retention.

question: Why do doctors and nurses sometimes give patients two or more medications at the same time?

options.A: To achieve a better therapeutic advantage for the patient
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing separate prescriptions
options.C: To completely eliminate the need for patient monitoring
options.D: To speed up the physical breakdown of tablets in the stomach

explanation: Great question! Sometimes teamwork makes the dream work—combining meds (like for high blood pressure) helps control an illness much better than using just one drug alone.

question: A hospital pharmacy prices an antibiotic by adding up the supplier price, shipping fees, storage power, and dispensing salaries. What costing approach is this?

options.A: Subsidized emergency pricing
options.B: Full operational cost recovery
options.C: Manufacturer retail pricing
options.D: Direct cost only approach

explanation: Spot on! Including both the price of the drug and all overhead expenses ensures the fund gets back every kobo spent to deliver care.

question: Which skin gland makes an oily substance called sebum to keep your hair and skin soft?

options.A: Eccrine sweat gland
options.B: Apocrine sweat gland
options.C: Ceruminous gland
options.D: Sebaceous gland

explanation: You're doing great! Sebaceous glands are our natural oil glands, usually attached to hair follicles, keeping our skin waterproof and moisturized.

question: Why is mixed feeding (breast milk plus other foods or water) discouraged for infants exposed to HIV?

options.A: It damages the infant's immature gut lining and increases transmission risk.
options.B: It is too expensive for families living in rural communities.
options.C: It prevents the baby from ever developing taste preferences.
options.D: It causes immediate allergic reactions in all newborn infants.

explanation: Introducing other liquids or foods irritates the baby's gut wall, making it much easier for the HIV virus in breast milk to enter the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h7)

question: What is the minimum legal age of marriage stipulated by the Nigerian Child Rights Act?

options.A: 15 years
options.B: 21 years
options.C: 18 years
options.D: 16 years

explanation: The Child Rights Act designates any individual under 18 years as a child and prohibits their marriage. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h4)

question: Why do skeletal muscles get bigger when someone does heavy weightlifting regularly?

options.A: Cellular hypertrophy occurs due to increased functional demand
options.B: Metaplasia transforms fat tissue directly into muscle tissue
options.C: Atrophy removes damaged proteins to make space for fluid
options.D: Hyperplasia creates brand new muscle fibers in the tissue

explanation: You're crushing this! Since muscle fibers don't easily make brand new cells, the existing cells bulk up (hypertrophy) to handle the heavy workload.

question: What is the dangerous practice of using the same syringe barrel for more than one patient called?

options.A: Syringe reuse
options.B: Z-track administration
options.C: Aseptic transfer
options.D: Vial reconstitution

explanation: You nailed it! Reusing syringes—even if you change the needle—transfers microscopic amounts of blood and fluids between patients, spreading serious infections. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h3)

question: How does adding a little glucose to oral rehydration solution help the body absorb water?

options.A: Glucose creates a thick barrier that stops water from leaving the body
options.B: Glucose binds with sodium to pull water across the gut wall together
options.C: Glucose makes the drink taste sweet so the child will drink more
options.D: Glucose feeds the good bacteria so they can repair the damaged bowel

explanation: It's like a team effort! Sodium and glucose hitch a ride together on the same transport protein. As glucose is absorbed, it pulls sodium and water right along with it into the bloodstream.

question: When does normal breast engorgement usually happen after a mother gives birth?

options.A: At six weeks postpartum
options.B: Day three to five
options.C: Immediately after birth
options.D: At two weeks postpartum

explanation: This is the time when mature milk comes in and blood flow to the breasts peaks. A totally normal part of the journey!

question: A nurse manager needs to buy daily supplies of syringes and gauze. Under which budget category do these routine expenses fall?

options.A: Investment budget
options.B: Operating budget
options.C: Capital budget
options.D: Construction budget

explanation: Routine, day-to-day operational costs like medical supplies and staff salaries are managed through the operating budget. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h3)

question: How do vaccines protect the human body against specific diseases?

options.A: Destroying all bacteria currently living in the gut
options.B: Increasing the overall body temperature to kill viruses
options.C: Stimulating antibody production without causing illness
options.D: Providing permanent chemical antibiotics in the blood

explanation: Spot on! Vaccines introduce harmless pieces or weakened parts of a germ so your immune system can safely learn to fight it without getting you sick.

question: What is the main feature of a correlational study?

options.A: Variables are not manipulated by the researcher
options.B: Random assignment is used for all participants
options.C: A specific medication is tested on patients
options.D: Only laboratory animals are studied

explanation: Spot on! In correlational studies, we simply observe natural relationships without changing or controlling things ourselves. You've got this!

question: What exactly do we mean by a "food myth" in healthcare?

options.A: A dietary belief that lacks scientific support
options.B: An official government nutrition guideline
options.C: A modern recipe created by clinical dietitians
options.D: A strict medical prescription for a disease

explanation: Food myths are unverified ideas about what food does to the body, passed along without scientific proof. Don't worry, once you spot them in clinical practice, they become much easier to address!

question: Why do waterborne diseases like cholera often spike during the rainy season in many Nigerian communities?

options.A: Rainfall increases the population of adult malaria-carrying mosquitoes
options.B: Cold weather lowers overall human immunity against intestinal parasites
options.C: Heavy rains can wash surface waste and sewage into vulnerable drinking water sources
options.D: Humidity causes airborne bacteria to multiply rapidly in closed indoor spaces

explanation: Exactly right. Heavy floods easily mix surface waste into community water supplies, increasing the risk of waterborne illnesses.

question: During the active phase of the first stage of labour, how often should you listen to the baby's heart rate?

options.A: Every 30 minutes
options.B: Only after membranes rupture
options.C: Every 2 hours
options.D: Every 5 minutes

explanation: Keep it up! Checking the fetal heart rate every 30 minutes helps you catch any signs of distress early and keep both mom and baby safe.

question: What is the main goal of having a "just culture" in a hospital?

options.A: Allowing senior doctors to break hospital rules without consequences
options.B: Ensuring that every single staff member receives the exact same salary
options.C: Punishing every nurse immediately when a minor paperwork error happens
options.D: Encouraging staff to report mistakes openly without fear of unfair punishment

explanation: Spot on! When nurses and staff feel safe speaking up about errors, the whole hospital becomes safer for everyone.

question: A nurse manager focuses only on cutting hospital operational costs while the ward nurses focus on getting overtime pay. What does this situation highlight?

options.A: A complete absence of any nursing documentation
options.B: That organisational objectives and personal objectives are always identical
options.C: That nurses do not care about patient care at all
options.D: A difference in focus between organisational and personal objectives

explanation: Management looks at the facility's budget (organisational), while staff nurses look at their own earnings and welfare (personal). Their focus is simply different here!

question: What term describes the abnormal body fat changes sometimes seen with long-term HIV and treatment?

options.A: Anasarca
options.B: Lipodystrophy
options.C: Cachexia
options.D: Sarcopenia

explanation: Lipodystrophy is when body fat shifts—some areas like the face and limbs lose fat, while the belly or back of the neck accumulates it.

question: How does a 'just culture' respond when a nurse makes an honest, accidental error?

options.A: It requires the nurse to pay out-of-pocket for any hospital damages
options.B: It mandates immediate termination of employment to protect patients
options.C: It treats the error as a signal to examine and fix the underlying system
options.D: It ignores the incident completely to avoid creating paperwork

explanation: A just culture knows good nurses make mistakes. Instead of pointing fingers, it asks: 'How can we fix the system so this doesn't happen again?'

question: What happens when a quality improvement project is launched without proper resources or support?

options.A: The hospital automatically gets federal grant money
options.B: Doctors take over all nursing documentation
options.C: Staff experience severe frustration and burnout, leading to project failure
options.D: Patients recover instantly with zero complications

explanation: Right! Without tools, time, and backing, new projects just pile extra stress onto already exhausted nurses. Support is everything.

question: What is a common myth used to justify FGM regarding hygiene?

options.A: Clipping the tissue improves daily personal hygiene efficiency
options.B: Uncut female genitalia are considered dirty and masculine
options.C: Surgical removal prevents all future skin infections
options.D: Natural anatomy causes unpleasant odors during adolescence

explanation: You got it! A widespread cultural myth falsely labels natural female anatomy as unclean.

question: Why is it risky to diagnose a nutrition problem based only on lab test results?

options.A: Patients refuse to provide samples for repeated nutritional screening.
options.B: Nutritional deficiencies never show up in blood or urine tests.
options.C: Many non-nutritional factors like hydration and disease skew the results.
options.D: Laboratory equipment is notoriously inaccurate in modern hospitals.

explanation: Always look at the whole patient! Things like fluid balance, infections, and medications can completely change lab outcomes independently of what the patient ate.

question: Why don't diaphragms and cervical caps protect very well against skin-to-skin STIs like HPV?

options.A: They leave the vaginal walls and external skin exposed
options.B: They allow semen to leak freely around the sides of the device
options.C: They dissolve too quickly when exposed to bodily fluids
options.D: They absorb viral particles and push them directly into the uterus

explanation: Correct! Because they only cover the cervix, surrounding skin and vaginal walls are still exposed to touch-based viruses. Great clinical insight!

question: A husband accompanies his pregnant wife to antenatal care. What should the nurse encourage him to learn?

options.A: Counsel other couples in the waiting room.
options.B: Learn about pregnancy danger signs and birth preparedness.
options.C: Perform a physical abdominal examination on his wife.
options.D: Prescribe prenatal vitamins to prevent anemia.

explanation: Teaching partners about warning signs ensures they can act quickly if an emergency happens. Wonderful!

question: Medication errors rise because a new drug pump has a confusing keypad. What is the best corrective action?

options.A: Suspending all medication administration duties for junior nurses
options.B: Decreasing the number of patients assigned to each shift nurse
options.C: Issuing official written warning letters to every nurse on the ward
options.D: Redesigning the workflow and retraining all nurses on the new keypad

explanation: Since the equipment itself is the problem, proper training and workflow adjustments directly fix the root cause.

question: What is the term for the separation of the front abdominal wall muscles that often happens during pregnancy?

options.A: Herniated disc
options.B: Carpal tunnel
options.C: Diastasis recti
options.D: Muscular dystrophy

explanation: Diastasis recti is simply the parting of the large front abdominal muscles to make room for the growing uterus. A very common finding in midwifery!

question: What is the preferred gentle way to clear the uterus in an early pregnancy loss up to 14 weeks?

options.A: Diagnostic laparoscopy
options.B: Manual Vacuum Aspiration
options.C: Cesarean section delivery
options.D: Total abdominal hysterectomy

explanation: Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA) is safe, quick, and very effective for early evacuation with fewer complications.

question: What is the primary focus of microbiology in nursing practice?

options.A: Synthesizing new pharmaceutical drugs in the ward
options.B: Calculating precise fluid balance for dehydrated patients
options.C: Understanding microscopic organisms and how they spread
options.D: Operating advanced diagnostic laboratory machinery

explanation: Microbiology studies tiny organisms like bacteria and viruses so nurses can understand how they cause disease and how to stop them. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why is it clinically important for nurses to separate biological sex from gender?

options.A: Gender is the only factor that matters for prescribing medications safely
options.B: Biological sex has no impact on a person's health outcomes whatsoever
options.C: Physical examinations are entirely unrelated to the concept of gender
options.D: Patients have both biological health needs and social experiences that affect care

explanation: Recognizing both biological and social dimensions ensures that nurses address the complete health profile of every patient without making false assumptions. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T1#GNS312_U4_T1_h2)

question: Which discovery marked the beginning of the antibiotic era in the 20th century?

options.A: Aspirin
options.B: Morphine
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Penicillin

explanation: Alexander Fleming's discovery of penicillin opened the antibiotic era, providing a powerful weapon against deadly bacterial infections. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T1#GNS125_U1_T1_h5)

question: How does great community health nursing help ease the burden on big tertiary hospitals in Nigeria?

options.A: By restricting patient movement from rural areas into big cities
options.B: By preventing and treating illnesses early at the local level before they become severe
options.C: By turning primary health centers into major surgical teaching hospitals
options.D: By replacing doctors with nurses in emergency rooms nationwide

explanation: Fantastic! Catching and treating issues early in the neighborhood keeps patients healthy and keeps those big tertiary hospitals from getting too crowded.

question: What is a major cause of waterborne and vector-borne diseases in local communities?

options.A: Excessive availability of modern private clinics
options.B: Inadequate portable water and poor waste disposal
options.C: Over-reliance on indoor physical exercise equipment
options.D: Strict adherence to universal sterile protocols

explanation: You got it! Without safe water and proper trash or sewage disposal, germs spread quickly and cause waterborne and insect-spread illnesses.

question: How is the pia mater different from the dura mater?

options.A: The pia mater forms venous sinuses, while the dura mater creates spiderweb trabeculae.
options.B: The pia mater floats freely in the skull, while the dura mater attaches to the spinal cord.
options.C: The pia mater sits outside the skull bone, while the dura mater sits inside the brain tissue.
options.D: The pia mater is delicate and follows brain contours, while the dura mater is tough and thick.

explanation: Think of extremes: the pia mater is super delicate and hugs the brain closely, while the dura mater is thick, tough, and sits on the outside.

question: As shock becomes more severe and progressive, what acid-base imbalance usually develops?

options.A: Respiratory alkalosis
options.B: Respiratory acidosis
options.C: Metabolic acidosis
options.D: Metabolic alkalosis

explanation: With lactic acid piling up and the body struggling to clear waste products, the blood's pH drops, leading directly to metabolic acidosis.

question: Where does the growing uterus usually push the stomach during pregnancy?

options.A: Downward and deep into the pelvis
options.B: Upward and to the left
options.C: Forward against the anterior abdominal wall
options.D: Directly backward against the spine

explanation: As the baby grows and takes up space below, the stomach gets nudged upward and slightly to the left. Makes sense when you picture it!

question: A patient who is severely dehydrated is most at risk of experiencing what?

options.A: Immediate thickening of bone tissue matrices
options.B: Rapid overproduction of red blood cells
options.C: Impaired kidney function and electrolyte imbalance
options.D: Excessive accumulation of dense adipose tissue

explanation: When water levels drop too low, blood volume decreases, placing stress on the kidneys and messing up vital body salts (electrolytes).

question: Which service would you most expect to find at a local primary health care center?

options.A: Sub-specialty pediatric neurology consultations
options.B: Advanced cancer chemotherapy and radiation therapy
options.C: Routine childhood immunization and antenatal care
options.D: Complex open-heart surgical procedures

explanation: Primary health centers focus heavily on community wellness. That means giving babies their routine vaccines and supporting mothers with antenatal care every day!

question: Why do low-income households frequently purchase highly processed foods?

options.A: Government food programs forbid buying fresh produce
options.B: They provide cheap calories that quickly relieve hunger
options.C: They contain more vitamins than fresh vegetables
options.D: They spoil much slower than natural foods

explanation: Processed foods packed with sugar and fat are inexpensive and filling, making them an economical choice for families with tight budgets. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T020#GNS227_U2_T020_h2)

question: How do most drugs travel from a pregnant mother to her baby?

options.A: Direct swallowing of amniotic fluid
options.B: Filtration through the fetal kidneys
options.C: Active pumping by the umbilical cord
options.D: Simple diffusion across the placenta

explanation: Medicines in the mother's bloodstream mostly cross over the placenta easily through simple diffusion to reach the baby. You've got this!

question: Which common condition causes physical blockage and urinary retention in older men?

options.A: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
options.B: Glomerular nephritis
options.C: Chronic kidney failure
options.D: Urinary tract infection

explanation: An enlarged prostate gland squeezes the pipe (urethra), making it physically hard for urine to flow out of the bladder. Keep up the great practice!

question: How does applying knowledge of community structure change the way you deliver healthcare?

options.A: It shifts care from something imposed on people to a collaborative partnership
options.B: It removes the need for community health clinics in rural areas
options.C: It replaces professional nurses with traditional birth attendants completely
options.D: It forces patients to obey hospital rules without asking questions

explanation: You aren't just bossing people around; you are teaming up with them! Understanding the community turns healthcare delivery into a wonderful partnership built on trust.

question: Which of these action verbs should you avoid in a research objective because it is too vague?

options.A: To appreciate
options.B: To measure
options.C: To identify
options.D: To compare

explanation: Words like 'appreciate' or 'understand' are feelings—they are too subjective and impossible to measure accurately in a study. Stick to concrete verbs! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h6)

question: How does endocrine signaling mostly differ from the nervous system?

options.A: Endocrine organs use ducts to release chemicals.
options.B: Nervous responses use hormones instead of electricity.
options.C: Endocrine responses are slower and last longer.
options.D: Nervous signals target every cell in the body at once.

explanation: You got it! While nervous system signals flash by in a split second, endocrine signals travel through the blood and take their time to create lasting effects.

question: What is the standard first-line medication for treating long-term hypothyroidism?

options.A: Levothyroxine
options.B: Propylthiouracil
options.C: Methimazole
options.D: Propranolol

explanation: Correct! Levothyroxine is a synthetic hormone that safely replaces what the natural thyroid isn't making enough of.

question: How has our view of leadership in healthcare changed over time?

options.A: From team collaboration to absolute individual control by doctors
options.B: From flexible behaviors to rigid, unchanging personal traits
options.C: From clinical skills to purely financial management tasks
options.D: From fixed personal traits to flexible behaviors and situational responses

explanation: We used to think leaders were just born with special traits. Now, we know good leaders adapt their style to fit whatever is happening on the ward!

question: What do chemical indicator strips placed on a sterile pack actually tell the nurse?

options.A: The autoclave machine is fully repaired and working
options.B: The package was exposed to the required temperature or steam
options.C: The instruments inside have no rust or organic debris
options.D: All bacteria inside the pack are completely dead

explanation: Chemical indicators change color to show heat exposure, but they do not guarantee that the required time or conditions killed all germs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h4)

question: What is an organ made of?

options.A: Individual atoms bonded tightly into complex organic molecules
options.B: A collection of identical cells performing the exact same task
options.C: Two or more different types of tissues working together
options.D: Multiple organ systems functioning inside a single body cavity

explanation: Think of an organ like a team! It takes different tissue types working together—like muscle and lining tissues—to get a big job done. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h2)

question: What happens to an ATP molecule after it gives energy to a cell?

options.A: It loses a phosphate group and turns into ADP
options.B: It gains an extra nitrogen atom and becomes a lipid
options.C: It splits entirely into four separate water molecules
options.D: It binds permanently to a red blood cell for transport

explanation: When ATP spends its energy, it releases one of its phosphate groups and becomes ADP (adenosine diphosphate). It is like a spent battery waiting to be recharged!

question: Which serious infection can easily spread by sharing unsterilized blades during scarification?

options.A: Typhoid fever
options.B: Common malaria
options.C: Hepatitis B
options.D: Simple cholera

explanation: Exactly! Unclean cutting tools transfer blood-borne viruses like Hepatitis B and HIV directly from person to person. Safety first!

question: Why is dragging a patient straight across bedsheets a bad idea for their skin?

options.A: It completely blocks the production of natural skin oils
options.B: It forces moisture deep into the subcutaneous fat layer
options.C: It creates friction and shear forces that damage skin and blood vessels
options.D: It causes an immediate drop in the patient's systemic blood pressure

explanation: Correct! Pulling someone across rough sheets creates friction and tears tiny blood vessels underneath. Always lift, never drag!

question: Which joint is looked at most often using an arthroscope?

options.A: Knee
options.B: Hip
options.C: Elbow
options.D: Wrist

explanation: The knee is the star of arthroscopy! Sports injuries involving the menisci and ligaments happen here all the time, making it the most common site for this scope.

question: Why are young women biologically more vulnerable to catching sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Faster overall blood circulation to the lower abdomen
options.B: Increased acidity of the normal vaginal flora
options.C: A higher resting body temperature in the pelvic region
options.D: The large area of mucous membrane in the reproductive tract

explanation: Think of the delicate lining inside the female reproductive tract—it has a large surface area that makes it easy for bacteria and viruses to settle in.

question: What action should a nurse take when a sharps container reaches its designated fill line?

options.A: Leave it open on the counter until the end of the working week
options.B: Seal and close the container securely for safe disposal
options.C: Push the needles down firmly with a gloved hand to create more space
options.D: Transfer some of the used needles into a regular plastic trash bag

explanation: Containers must be closed and replaced once they reach the fill line to prevent accidental overflows and needle injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h6)

question: Which layer of the placenta is directly bathed in the mother's blood?

options.A: Fetal endothelium
options.B: Connective tissue
options.C: Syncytiotrophoblast
options.D: Cytotrophoblast

explanation: The syncytiotrophoblast is the brave outer layer that sits right in the maternal blood pool, handling nutrient and gas exchange for the baby. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T5#GNS121_U6_T5_h2)

question: Why is Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) ranked at the very bottom of safety controls?

options.A: It relies heavily on human behavior and fails if not worn correctly
options.B: It completely removes the hazard from the work environment
options.C: It is the only method approved by hospital management
options.D: It is always more expensive than engineering controls

explanation: PPE is just a barrier—if you forget to put it on properly or take it off carelessly, you are still exposed. That's why it's our last line of defense, not the first!

question: Why does the systemic circulation require higher pressure than the pulmonary circulation?

options.A: It has to travel a much longer distance through the whole body
options.B: It must push blood upward against gravity at all times
options.C: It connects directly to the high-pressure kidney filters
options.D: It handles both oxygen and carbon dioxide simultaneously
